body:
## Why

gpui dispatches node key handlers by the raw key string, which includes single printable punctuation keys (`?`, `/`, `[`, `]`, `-`, `=`). Both `on_key_value` and `on("key:<name>")` rejected every non-alphanumeric key name, so keyboard-first UIs could not bind help on `?`, filter on `/`, or steppers on `[` `]` — exactly the keys desktop apps rely on. Found while porting tobi/disktree to a rhai skin (disktree-rhai).

## What

- `on_key_value`: names accept printable ASCII except the reserved `:` namespace separator (lowercased, as before).
- `validate_node_event_name`: general event names keep the snake_case rule; only the `key:` segment widens to printable ASCII.
- Script-boundary tests for both accept and reject directions.
- `docs/actions-and-keybindings.md`: new "Node key handlers" section documenting the rule (named keys, punctuation, `:` reserved, no modifiers — chords stay host-bound).

## Verification

`cargo test -p gpui-rhai --lib` — 439 passed (2 new). `cargo clippy -p gpui-rhai --lib` clean.
title: feat(node): accept punctuation key names in key handlers
